summary: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs, e.g., PCV13, PCV15, PCV20) contain purified capsular polysaccharides from several Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes each covalently linked (conjugated) to a carrier protein such as CRM197 (a nontoxic diphtheria toxin variant). Conjugation converts the polysaccharide into a T-cell-dependent antigen, generating a strong antibody response with immunologic memory even in infants and young children, in whom plain polysaccharide vaccines are poorly immunogenic. PCVs are part of the routine infant immunization schedule (given as a primary series with a booster) and are recommended for older children, adults 65 years and older, and younger adults with conditions that increase the risk of invasive pneumococcal disease. They protect against invasive pneumococcal disease (bacteremia, meningitis) and pneumonia caused by the included serotypes and reduce nasopharyngeal carriage. The vaccine is given as a 0.5 mL intramuscular injection. It is generally well tolerated; injection-site reactions, fever, irritability, and drowsiness are common in children, and local reactions and myalgia in adults. Serious reactions such as anaphylaxis are rare. Current schedules sequence PCV with pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) in certain groups.
indications: Active immunization for the prevention of invasive disease and pneumonia caused by the Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes contained in the vaccine
Routine immunization of infants and young children as part of the childhood schedule (primary series plus booster)
Immunization of adults 65 years of age and older

Immunization of children and adults at increased risk of pneumococcal disease (e.g., asplenia/sickle cell disease, immunocompromise, chronic heart, lung, liver, or kidney disease, diabetes, cochlear implants, cerebrospinal fluid leaks)

dosage.n: Followed by a booster dose; follow the national/ACIP schedule for the specific PCV product

dosage.t: 1 or more doses by age and history
dosage.n: Number of doses depends on age at first dose and prior vaccination

dosage.n: Dosing/sequence depends on the PCV product (e.g., PCV20 alone, or PCV15 followed by PPSV23) per current recommendations

moa: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine contains capsular polysaccharides of selected Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes, each chemically conjugated to an immunogenic carrier protein (e.g., CRM197). By covalently linking the polysaccharide to a protein, the vaccine recruits T-helper lymphocyte assistance, converting what would otherwise be a weak T-cell-independent polysaccharide response into a robust T-cell-dependent response. This generates high-affinity, serotype-specific anticapsular IgG antibodies, immunologic memory (B-memory cells enabling strong booster responses), and effective immunogenicity in infants under 2 years. The induced antibodies promote opsonophagocytosis and complement-mediated killing of pneumococci bearing the vaccine serotypes, conferring protection against invasive disease and reducing nasopharyngeal carriage (and thereby transmission).

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) after a previous dose of any pneumococcal conjugate vaccine or to any vaccine component, including diphtheria toxoid/CRM197 carrier protein
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness, with or without fever (defer until recovery)
Bleeding disorders or anticoagulation (take precautions for intramuscular injection)
Immunosuppression (response may be reduced; vaccination still recommended for protection)
monitor: Apnea in very premature infants after the first immunizations
Adherence to the correct age-based dosing schedule and PCV/PPSV23 sequencing

preg: There is no evidence that pneumococcal conjugate vaccines are harmful in pregnancy. They are not routinely recommended during pregnancy but may be given when a woman is at increased risk of pneumococcal disease and the benefit is judged to outweigh any theoretical risk; follow current guidance.
lact: Vaccine components are not expected to be present in or affect breast milk, and the vaccine is considered compatible with breastfeeding. Breastfeeding is not a contraindication to maternal vaccination, and it does not impair the infant's response to their own vaccination.
renal: Chronic kidney disease, nephrotic syndrome, and dialysis are indications for pneumococcal vaccination because of increased disease risk; standard 0.5 mL dosing applies. The antibody response may be somewhat reduced in advanced renal disease.
hepatic: Chronic liver disease (including cirrhosis) is an indication for pneumococcal vaccination; standard dosing applies and no hepatic dose adjustment is needed.

major: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, radiation, biologics) - may reduce the antibody response; vaccinate before immunosuppression where feasible
moderate: Pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) - give in the recommended sequence and interval (generally PCV first, then PPSV23 after a specified interval) rather than at the same visit
minor: Other inactivated or live vaccines may generally be co-administered at separate sites per schedule
interactions.alcohol: No interaction with alcohol; chronic alcoholism is itself a high-risk indication for vaccination.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine laboratory monitoring is required; serologic confirmation of response is not generally needed.

common: Injection-site reactions - pain, redness, swelling, induration
serious: Marked local reaction with extensive limb swelling
emergency: Anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat, hives, hypotension, collapse)
Apnea or marked breathing pauses in a young/premature infant after vaccination

monitoring: Observe the patient after vaccination for immediate hypersensitivity reactions and syncope
Monitor very premature infants for apnea after the initial doses
Ensure correct age-based dosing schedule and proper sequencing/interval with PPSV23 where indicated
Document vaccination and risk indications for completion of the series and any sequential PPSV23 dose
counsel: This vaccine protects against serious pneumococcal infections such as meningitis, bloodstream infection, and pneumonia caused by several common strains
Children receive it as a series of injections; some adults need it once or in sequence with another pneumococcal vaccine - your provider will advise the schedule
Soreness, redness, or swelling where the shot was given, along with mild fever, fussiness, or sleepiness in young children, are common and short-lived
It does not protect against pneumococcal strains not in the vaccine or other causes of pneumonia
Tell your provider about any severe allergy to a previous pneumococcal or diphtheria-containing vaccine, and seek help for difficulty breathing, swelling, or hives
pk: Protective antibody responses develop over roughly 2-4 weeks after a dose
Peak serotype-specific antibody levels within about 1 month after completing the recommended doses
Not applicable (vaccine - induces an immune response rather than measurable drug levels)
Conjugate vaccines induce immunologic memory; antibody levels persist for years and boost on re-exposure
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (35-46 F); do not freeze; discard if frozen; protect per label
pearls: Conjugation to a carrier protein makes the response T-cell-DEPENDENT, giving immunologic memory and effective immunization in infants <2 years - the key advantage over plain polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23)
PCV is part of the routine infant series (primary doses plus a booster) and reduces nasopharyngeal carriage, producing herd protection
For adults >=65 and at-risk adults, follow current ACIP/national guidance on which PCV (e.g., PCV15 or PCV20) and whether sequential PPSV23 is needed
Protects only against the serotypes in the formulation; does not cover non-vaccine serotypes
Watch for apnea in very premature infants after the first doses; anaphylaxis is rare but treat immediately
Coordinate timing/sequence of PCV and PPSV23 per schedule rather than giving them at the same visit
missed: If a dose in the series is delayed or missed, give it at the next opportunity - there is no need to restart the series; resume according to the catch-up schedule. For adults due for a sequential dose with PPSV23, administer it at the recommended interval. Follow the national/ACIP catch-up guidance for the specific product.
overdose: Overdose is not a meaningful concern for this single-dose-by-visit vaccine. Inadvertent administration of more than the recommended dose, or giving doses closer together than recommended, chiefly increases the likelihood and severity of local injection-site reactions and fever. Management is supportive and symptomatic.
